questions.question:
**In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. **

My elder son deals with (1)/ spare parts and manages (2)/ his bread and butter. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• There is an error in the first part of the sentence.
 
• This could be easily found out **when the second part is read in continuation **to the first part. 
 
• The phrase **'deal with' **means **to do something about (a person or thing that causes a problem or difficult situation)** ​
 
 
• *The government **dealt **harshly **with **the rebels.*
 
• *I'll **deal with** you later.*
 
 
 
• *​*The phrase '**deal in**' means* ***to buy and sell (something) as a business.**
 
 
• *He **deals in** rare books.*
 
 
 
• Hence, **'deals with**' will be **replaced **by **'deals in'**.
 
• Hence, the correct sentence is**- 'My elder son deals in spare parts and manages his bread and butter.'**

Hence, the correct answer will be Option 1.

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Sneha was accused for her husband's murder but the court found her not guilty and acquitted her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'for her husband's murder'- the error lies in this part.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the first part of the sentence.
 
• In the first part, 'for' has to be replaced with 'of' as the verb 'accuse' takes the preposition 'of' after it. 
 
• Hence the correct option is option 1.

 

**Correct sentence:** Sneha was accused **of her husband's murder** but the court found her not guilty and acquitted her

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

My sister's marriage passed ________ peacefully.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The filler for this should be a culminating verb for the marriage procession. 
 
• Now a marriage procession is a ceremony which starts ”on” and passes “off”.
 
• A function, ceremony or ritual cannot be passed “away” or “by” as they are not material living beings. 
 
 
• Example:-* *
 
• *The old woman **passed away** quietly*
 
• *Don't let this opportunity **pass (you) by!***
 
• *Have both your parents **passed on**?*
 
 
 
• These verbs are used for people or things. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

**Pass off**

Meaning: Happen, Misrepresent something

Example: The millennium passed off without any disasters, He tried to pass off the imitation Rolex as genuine.

 

**Pass on**

Meaning: Convey or communicate, Skip or decline, Die

Example: Can you pass on the information next time you see him?, I’ll pass on dessert, thanks, His uncle passed on last year.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

There are _____ books on computer science in your school library, so you need to purchase them from the market.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Few**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 
 
According to the rules of using** few, a few, little and a little, **we have to consider whether the noun is **countable **or uncountable, and whether the meaning is **positive **or **negative**.

 
 
• 
 
**Books **are countable nouns, so we have to use **few **or **a few.**

 
 
• 
 
**Few **means **almost none and has a negative meaning,** while **a few** means some and has a **positive **meaning.

 
 
• For Example:
 
 
• A few members of the family leave their hometown each year.
 
• **Few **members of the family leave their hometown each year.
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 
Therefore, the correct word to fill in the blank is: **few**

 
 
• 
 
This is because the sentence implies that **there are not many books on computer science in the school library, **which is a **negative **situation.

 
 
• 
 
If we use** a few,** it would mean that there are **some books, which is not the case**.

 
 
• 
 
The sentence would be: *There are **few **books on computer science in your school library, so you need to purchase them from the market*

 
 
• Hence, the correct **option is 3.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Raucous
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. Dulcet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Raucous"** means making or constituting a disturbingly harsh and loud noise. (कर्कश)

 
 
• **Example:** The raucous laughter from the party could be heard from down the street.
 
 
 
• **"Dulcet"** refers to something that is sweet and soothing (often used ironically), especially of sound. (मधुर)
 
 
• **Example:** The dulcet tones of the lullaby helped the baby fall asleep.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Dulcet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Hoarse** (रूखा): Sounding rough and harsh, typically as the result of a sore throat or of shouting.

 
 
• **Example:** His voice was hoarse after shouting at the concert all night.
 
 
 
• **Jarring** (झंझट): Incongruous in a striking or shocking way; clashing.
 
 
• **Example:** The jarring noise of the alarm clock jolted him awake.
 
 
 
• **Torrent** (प्रवाह): A strong and fast-moving stream of water or other liquid.
 
 
• **Example:** The heavy rain turned the stream into a raging torrent.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Predilection
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. Enmity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Predilection"** means a preference or special liking for something; a bias in favor of something. (पूर्वाग्रह)

 
 
• **Example:** Her predilection for classical music was evident in her vast collection of symphonies.
 
 
 
• **"Enmity"** refers to the state or feeling of being actively opposed or hostile to someone or something. (दुश्मनी)
 
 
• **Example:** There has always been enmity between the two rival factions.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Enmity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Inclination** (रुझान): A person's natural tendency or urge to act or feel in a particular way.

 
 
• **Example:** She had a strong inclination towards the arts from a young age.
 
 
 
• **Enduring** (सहना): Lasting over a period of time; durable.
 
 
• **Example:** Their enduring friendship spanned several decades.
 
 
 
• **Domicile** (निवास): The country or place that a person treats as their permanent home, or lives in and has a substantial connection with.
 
 
• **Example:** He moved to a new domicile in the city after getting the new job.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

I wish I (was) a superman.
questions.solution:
‘**If I were…**’ and ‘**If I was…**’ are **both correct** forms to use when referring to a hypothetical situation. (Second Conditional/ Unreal Present).

The use of ‘were’ is considered more formal. This form is called the ‘Past Subjunctive’ and is often used after:

 
• if
 
• as if
 
• wish

 
• If Superman were here, he could help you.
 
• He speaks to me as if he were the President.
 
• I wish Jack were more reliable.

 

However, ‘I/he/she/it was’ is also an accepted form and is used in informal conversation:

 
• If Superman was here, he could help you.
 
• He speaks to me as if he was the President.
 
• I wish Jack was more reliable.

 

The only time we don’t normally use ‘was’ is in the fixed expression ‘If I were you’:

 
• If I were you, I’d look up Subjunctive in English Grammar in Use.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the phrase. **

A perception without objective reality
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Hallucination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Hallucination"** means an experience involving the apparent perception of something not present. (मतिभ्रम)

 
 
• **Example:** After days without sleep, he began to experience vivid hallucinations.
 
 
 
• **"Perception without objective reality"** refers to experiencing something that is not actually present in the environment. (वह धारणा जो वास्तविकता में मौजूद नहीं है)
 
 
• **Example:** Seeing water in a desert due to a mirage is a classic case of perception without objective reality.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Hallucination**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Cynicism** (नीयत में खोट): The belief that people are motivated purely by self-interest rather than acting for honorable or unselfish reasons.

 
 
• **Example:** His cynicism makes it hard for him to trust anyone.
 
 
 
• **Illusion** (भ्रम): A deceptive appearance or impression; something that is wrongly perceived by the senses.
 
 
• **Example:** The magician’s trick created the illusion of a disappearing act.
 
 
 
• **Optimism** (आशावाद): Hopefulness and confidence about the future or the success of something.
 
 
• **Example:** Her optimism helps her overcome difficult challenges with ease.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of ****labelled**** sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

P- Granted, a political defection is increasingly less an act of ideological deﬁance than one of pure opportunism. 

Q - Yet, for all it ﬂaws, the current law recognizes and respects one fundamental principle: The right to dissent. 

R - A blanket ban on defection will weaken rather than strengthen democracy, in whose name it is being sought to be imposed. 

S - Granted also that it is illogical to allow a third of the party to split but not in a lesser number. 

2f:T
questions.solution:
In the given set of para-jumbled sentences, the first statement should be R which introduces the topic of the blanket ban of defection. Then, the following two statements are of the same form which helps in the development of the topic. These should be placed first P then S. 

The last statement, Q then culminates the topic with a conclusion. 

The correct option 1.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

After driving Dr. Bose to the hospital he dropped him at his guest house.

options.text: After being driven to the hospital Dr. Bose was dropped at his guest house.
After he had driven Dr. Bose to the hospital he had dropped him at his guest house.
After he was driving Dr. Bose to the hospital he was dropping him at his guest house.
Dr. Bose was being driven to the hospital ﬁrst and then he was being dropped at his guest house.

questions.solution: When transition is made from active to passive voice the tense or the meaning should not be changed at all. Since option 3 is not in the same meaning as the active voice, therefore, it is eliminated. Option 4 is not the correct transformation, it should be eliminated. Option 2 changes the tense in the second part of the sentence, thus making it incorrect too. The correct transformation is option 1.

questions.question:
** In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

I said to my friends, "let us go to a picnic for a change".

options.text: I asked my friends if they would go to a picnic for a change.
I asked my friends to go to a picnic for a change.
I permitted my friends to go to a picnic for a change.
I suggested to my friends that we should go to a picnic for a change.

questions.solution: In the given direct speech, the tone of the speaker is that of a suggestion and not a request. During transformation, the meaning or the essence of the speech should not be changed. Option 1 is more of a request and is not the correct indirect speech to the direct speech given. Option 2 is an order and it too, is not the correct transformation. Option 3 is also incorrect as no one asked the speaker for permission. The correct option is option 4.
